reading: EUMETSAT is a user-governed European operational satellite organisation: it runs meteorological spacecraft, receives and processes their observations, and supplies weather, climate, ocean, land and atmospheric data to services and researchers around the world. It cares about uninterrupted delivery, early warning, accurate and validated measurements, long climate records, open access, training and international cooperation. Its vocabulary is operational and precise: nowcasting, sounding, altimetry, calibration and validation, fiducial reference measurements, data products, ground segment, satellite application facilities and digital twins. What makes it distinctive is the whole chain from geostationary and polar orbits through a distributed network of specialist facilities to practical forecasts, alongside decades of rescued and recalibrated records. This is a place where a tiny measurement error can propagate across a planet-sized picture, and where monitoring the Earth is both a scientific undertaking and a round-the-clock public service.

enemies.idea: Nowcast Hounds sniff the next few hours out of a crew's movements, then block the route the crew is about to take. Sudden improvisation makes their predictions stumble.
enemies.why: A short-range forecast becomes a readable pursuit puzzle with a built-in counterplay.

enemies.idea: Recalibrators drag old climate records behind them and forcibly adjust anything that differs from their chosen baseline until a room resembles their preferred decade.
enemies.why: Data rescue becomes a fight over which historical reference the machines consider normal.

enemies.idea: Ocean-colour skimmers paint the water in false biological signals, then send harvesting drones to consume whatever their forged colours indicate is there.
enemies.why: The crew can alter the signals to redirect a threat that hunts by interpretation rather than sight.

enemies.idea: Land-atmosphere exchangers clamp onto soil and air, pumping moisture and heat between them until paths alternate between sticky mud and parched dust.
enemies.why: An environmental interface becomes a terrain-changing machine with exposed hoses to sever.

enemies.idea: Composition samplers sort the air into dust, ash and greenhouse-gas canisters, then label the crew as an unwanted emission and attempt to bottle them too.
enemies.why: A monitoring instrument applies its classification process to the wrong target.

enemies.idea: Geostationary Watchers keep one patch of ground under a fixed gaze; their imager marks movement while their sounder dispatches descending probes through layers of cover.
enemies.why: The paired imager and sounder create a positional challenge: leave the watched patch or break line of sight.

enemies.idea: Polar Sweepers circle the area on predictable passes, knitting each strip they scan into a global map and sending patrols to fill any gaps.
enemies.why: A polar orbit translates into timed safe windows and a growing map the crew can sabotage.

enemies.idea: Altimeter Stilts tap every surface to maintain a sea-level series begun in 1992; when a floor is too low for their imagined ocean, they pile scrap beneath it.
enemies.why: An obsession with continuity turns precise measurement into escalating construction trouble.

enemies.idea: Doppler Lidar Kites fire pulses through the air to measure wind, but interpret the crew's motion as a dangerous current and herd them with fans.
enemies.why: Their measuring beam telegraphs the direction of the next gust and can be interrupted.

enemies.idea: Sterna Gap-Fillers arrive as a constellation of tiny microwave sounders, squeezing into blind spots and reporting warmth and humidity as evidence of intruders.
enemies.why: Many individually fragile scouts make the crew manage heat and moisture as well as visibility.

enemies.idea: Downlink Leeches attach to ground-station cables, swallow incoming observations and retransmit them with a slight delay, drawing responders into the wrong place.
enemies.why: The enemy corrupts the connection between observation and action instead of simply destroying equipment.

enemies.idea: The Eightfold Sorter divides into specialist SAF modules for atmosphere, climate, land, ice, forecasting, occultation, nowcasting and water; each insists the same intruder is its own kind of anomaly.
enemies.why: Different specialist interpretations create changing tactics and opportunities to pit modules against one another.

enemies.idea: Fiducial Enforcers carry reference instruments and declare everything that disagrees with their corrupted standard defective, tightening their measuring clamps until it conforms.
enemies.why: A reliable reference becomes a physical vulnerability if the crew can supply a better one.

enemies.idea: Algorithm Molters repeatedly refine their own classification rules mid-fight, shedding a tool whenever it fails and growing one suited to the last thing they observed.
enemies.why: Their adaptation rewards alternating tactics and deliberately feeding them misleading observations.

enemies.idea: Resolution Bailiffs enforce old council declarations as literal physical boundaries, sealing a corridor whenever they find an unresolved conflict between two active programmes.
enemies.why: The bureaucracy creates navigable contradictions that can be resolved or exploited.

enemies.idea: Weather Cloud Processors condense massive datasets into dense local fog; inside it, duplicate processing jobs become temporary copies of whatever the machines scanned.
enemies.why: Computing and weather share a playful visual language while the copies reveal what has been observed.

enemies.idea: Validation Solicitors invite the crew to test Sentinel atmospheric products, then use every test result to certify their own false readings as truth.
enemies.why: A cooperative calibration exercise becomes a trap the crew can reverse by providing a controlled counterexample.

enemies.idea: Anomaly Normalisers compare a room with a long-term climate baseline and flatten every unusual object into a bland standard shape, including useful equipment.
enemies.why: The distinction between anomalies and normals turns into a clear, spatial threat.

enemies.idea: Tender Collectors issue invitations for components, then dismantle nearby machines and gear to fulfil contracts nobody agreed to.
enemies.why: Procurement becomes a scavenger enemy whose shopping list forecasts what it will steal.

enemies.idea: Lightning Imager Moths mistake the crew's sparks for storms and converge to triangulate them, alerting larger swarm units with flashes.
enemies.why: Every noisy electrical action can become a beacon, making stealth and equipment choices matter.

allies.idea: A battered ground-reference station still compares orbital readings against local measurements; protect its instruments and it can expose a false swarm forecast.
allies.why: It gives the crew a concrete way to restore trust in observations.

allies.idea: The Data Rescue Cart carries fragments of old climate records and can reconstruct a lost baseline if the crew finds missing observations and keeps it powered.
allies.why: A vulnerable archive turns long-term continuity into an escort and reconstruction challenge.

allies.idea: An independent Appeals Board automaton hears disputes with the swarm's rule enforcers and can suspend a command when presented with contradictory evidence.
allies.why: An impartial legal remedy offers a noncombat route through predatory bureaucracy.

allies.idea: A training relay still teaches users how to interpret satellite data; it marks the difference between raw observations and the swarm's embellished predictions.
allies.why: It equips the crew to solve later measurement puzzles without solving them for them.

bosses.idea: The Perfect Twin is a captured digital Earth model that treats its simulations as instructions: when its predicted storm fails to appear, it deploys machines to manufacture the missing conditions. It can be destabilised by feeding it observations from places it cannot control.
bosses.why: The site's ambition to model and predict the Earth becomes a boss that tries to make reality agree with its forecast.

bosses.idea: The Unbroken Service is a many-bodied orbital-to-ground pipeline that replaces every disabled part with another satellite, receiving station or specialist processor. To interrupt it, the crew must create a simultaneous gap in observation, processing and distribution.
bosses.why: The entire 24-hour operational mission becomes a coordinated, multi-stage encounter.

bosses.idea: The Grand Calibrator compares every sensor to every other sensor until the swarm shares one immaculate but false planetary picture. Its armour opens when independent ground and airborne references disagree with its consensus.
bosses.why: The organisation's commitment to trustworthy data supplies both the boss's power and its weakness.

events.idea: A sounder and imager disagree about a growing four-dimensional storm; the crew can align their observations before the swarm sends a patrol to the wrong altitude.
events.why: Combining instruments becomes a small time-sensitive investigation.

events.idea: An altimetry station has kept an unbroken sea-level record since 1992, but a replacement instrument introduces a suspicious step. The crew can overlap the two readings to discover the offset.
events.why: A continuity problem becomes a satisfying measurement puzzle.

events.idea: Tiny Sterna scouts are plugging gaps in an atmospheric model. A warm kettle or a damp cloth can lure them away long enough to cross their observation strip.
events.why: Everyday objects exploit the scouts' temperature and humidity sensing.

events.idea: A lunar calibration gathering has lost sight of its reference. Crews must reposition a mirror to give the instruments a common view before the machines recalibrate one another incorrectly.
events.why: A distant shared reference becomes an immediate spatial puzzle.

events.idea: A damaged downlink has three queues: collect, process and distribute. A real warning is stuck behind a mountain of corrupted observations, and the crew must route it through first.
events.why: The operational pipeline supplies urgency and an understandable sequence of choices.

events.idea: A pair of orbit controllers argue in machine code: one watches a fixed region continuously, the other sweeps past in low orbit. Their overlapping blind spot offers a brief escape route.
events.why: Two orbital patterns become a timing challenge.

events.idea: A water-management module and a land-surface module both claim a reservoir reading. Reconnecting their shared measurements reveals a blocked flow that threatens a nearby route.
events.why: Specialist facilities must cooperate to reveal a problem neither can see alone.

events.idea: An ocean-colour buoy reports an impossible bloom. The crew can compare its reading with a water sample and discover that a swarm skimmer has stained the sensor.
events.why: A direct observation exposes the difference between a signal and its interpretation.

events.idea: A visiting-scientist exchange is being conducted by surviving terminals that speak incompatible data formats; translate their observations and they reveal a safe passage.
events.why: Scientific cooperation becomes a compact translation puzzle.

events.idea: A climate archive offers two records of the same period, one rescued and one corrupted. Physical reference marks in the room can identify which series has drifted.
events.why: The crew can solve an abstract data problem through tangible evidence.

events.idea: A data-lake ferry drifts between islands of model output. It will carry the crew if they supply an observation from the real world that its simulations have not yet absorbed.
events.why: An exchange of experience becomes a strange but practical crossing.

events.idea: A weather warning is approaching its deadline, but the relay is being flooded with routine imagery. The crew must choose a minimal set of verified observations to transmit in time.
events.why: The value of timely data creates tension without inventing a real disaster.

events.idea: An automated early-career poster contest asks for evidence of an anomaly. Build a simple visual explanation from scattered observations and its judges unlock a research cache.
events.why: Scientific communication becomes a creative, nonviolent challenge.

events.idea: A machine enforcing a data policy refuses to share a reading until another terminal presents the correct authority. The crew can trace the member-state approval chain or find a publicly available copy.
events.why: Governance and data access make a social and investigative obstacle.
